descriptions.text: Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams. This is a stick. It's enchanted. It's not a wand, but when used correctly, it can do something truly magical.

recap.text: Dmitri Popov hands Donut a metal rod ten inches long, with what feels like a number seven at one end. Prepotente splashes a potion on a glass wall and pushes the stick into the wet spot, and it slides through like magic until it stops halfway. One tap of the hammer breaks the entire level into dust, and Cascadia screams over the announcement system.

beats.headline: Not a wand
beats.text: Dmitri Popov was ridiculously excited to finally meet Donut and hand his gift over, and unlike Imani he got no notice of an appeal. It is a metal rod about a quarter of an inch thick and ten inches long, apparently aluminium, though its description does not say, and from that description it seems connected to the hammer. Who's Cascadia? Carl asks. Mordecai shrugs: this kind of thing is usually named after past crawlers, bosses or places, and of the few Cascadias he can think of, only one is connected to the crawl. Then Carl's finger catches a slight imperfection at the end of the rod. It feels like a symbol. He thinks it is the number seven.
beats.gist: Dmitri Popov gives Donut a metal rod, and Carl feels what seems to be a seven on it.

beats.headline: Prepotente has been collecting clues
beats.text: At the masquerade Carl asks Prepotente when he last slept, and the goat insists on joining his party. Carl says no: talk to Katia, or start a party of his own and join the guild. It would only be for the rest of this floor, Prepotente says, so that they travel together to the start of the next. He has been collecting the clues, and Katia has told him about Donut's magical hammer and stick. Then a voice booms from the stage, Prepotente screams right in Carl's ear, and Carl bookmarks the whole thing until they are through the party.
beats.gist: Prepotente asks to join Carl's party for the masquerade floor, but Carl refuses and bookmarks the matter.

beats.headline: Through the glass like magic
beats.text: In the seventh floor's starting chamber, Prepotente explains himself. The level is built like a Prince Rupert's drop on a massive scale, and it is called the Great Race, which is also the name of a fairytale about a boy in a maze whose tunnels seal behind him. He asks Donut for the hammer and the magical stick and holds a thermometer to the glass; the whole tale, he says, is in the description of his mother's boots. He splashes a potion on the wall. When the countdown hits zero and Cascadia rushes through the rules, he pushes the stick into the wet spot, and it slides through like magic. Godsdamnit, Prepotente, Cascadia says. Don't do it. The stick stops halfway.
beats.gist: Prepotente pushes the stick into a potion-wetted wall; it slides through, then stops halfway when Cascadia objects.

beats.headline: The whole level breaks
beats.text: One tiny tap of the hammer, and a lightning pattern of fissures runs over the glass. Interesting, Prepotente says, his voice gone distant: he thought it would be instantaneous. Then the wall shatters, and not just that wall. The entire level explodes into fine dust, every crawler is sucked into the portals at the same time, and Carl and Donut flip head over toes into the stairwell. The last thing Carl hears is Cascadia screaming over the announcement system. He broke the whole level, Donut says in the marble chamber. All their sponsors came together to make sure he pulled it off, Carl answers.
beats.gist: Carl and Donut's Stick taps the glass, the level turns to dust, and they tumble into the stairwell.
